answer: Hardware cipher handshake binding. Each agent identity must solve a fresh challenge inside a boundary-scan chain physically unique to one fabricated chip, whose per-die key is fused at manufacture and unreadable externally. Registration accepts only signed replies from that die, recorded once per serial. An attacker must buy and solder a distinct chip for every identity, so forging a thousand agents costs a thousand dies plus board assembly, labor, and scrap. A reef of cloned identities collapses because no die signs twice; the ocean of traffic cannot counterfeit silicon,
